newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia government worried about monopolies.
newsitem.headline: Russia government worried about monopolies.

text.p: Russia's State Anti-Monopoly Committee is worried about the level of monopoly concentration in some industries, although telecommunications is not one of them, a committee official said on Monday.

Vladimir Belov, deputy chairman of the committee, told a news conference that about 750 companies dominate the Russian market, including about 250 factories dominating machine-building and between 80 and 85 factories dominating chemicals, oil refining and metallurgy.
"We are concerned about this," he said.
He added that he was especially worried by that between 3,500 and 4,500 regional companies that had dominating position on local markets.
He said competition was yet to develop in some sectors, including telecommunications.
He said the planned transfer of 38 percent of state-owned shares in Rostelekom to Svyazinvest holding company, would have no impact on competition in the industry.
He said that while Rostelekom controlled long-distance and international calls, Svyazinvest controlled local calls in the regions.
Besides, the low number of lines per capita and poor technology prevented the sector from becoming competitive.
"We must first raise the coverage of consumers and the technological side of it and then start setting up a competitive environment," he said.
